title: Sardinian Restaurants Ask Families to Put Phones Away
paragraphs: In many restaurants today, it is common to see families sitting at the same table while everyone looks at a phone or tablet. Now, a group of restaurants on the Italian island of Sardinia is trying to change this.

In November 2026, 15 restaurants across Sardinia began a one-month trial called "A tavola senza schermi," which means "At the table without screens." The project was launched by Anna Cau, Sardinia's ombudsman for children and teenagers, together with Fipe Confcommercio Sardegna, an organization that represents restaurants. At first, the organizers planned to involve eight restaurants, but more businesses volunteered to take part.

Under the project, families are asked to put away their phones during meals so that they can talk to each other face to face. If someone needs to make an exception, the family is encouraged to agree on it beforehand. If there is an urgent call, people should take it away from the table.

However, the project is not a strict ban. Instead, it asks parents to set a good example by putting away their own phones, too. Sometimes, parents give children devices to keep them busy while the adults eat, and the organizers want to discourage this.

To help families, the participating restaurants offer a "Reunion Kit." It was developed with advice from Italian pediatricians, and it contains games and drawing activities to keep children busy while they wait for their food. The kit also includes information about children's screen use and advice on how to manage technology at home.

The project has been introduced because of concerns about how much time children spend in front of screens. According to Emanuele Frongia, the president of Fipe Confcommercio Sardegna, conversation at the table is being replaced by silence when people focus on their phones.
Some people have pointed out that the project is not only about children. As one Italian newspaper noted, it is mainly adults who need to learn how to sit at the table without a phone.
